title: Unique centerwise descent of a finite equivariant toric tower to monoschemes
statement: Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme with finite affine cover, and let $X_0=\mathbf Q[M]$, with the component tori, normalized towers and saturated monoscheme blowups of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Let $(X_i,J_i)_{0\le i<n}$, with last scheme $X_n$, be a finite normalized blowup tower such that each coherent ring ideal $J_i$ is preserved by the original component tori acting on $X_i$, and its zero scheme is nowhere dense. Then there is a unique finite ordered saturated monoscheme blowup tower $M_n\to\cdots\to M_0=M$ lifting this centered tower: each $M_i$ is fine, torsion free and has a finite affine cover; its coherent center $I_i$ is nonempty on every component; and the canonical torus-equivariant identifications $X_i\simeq\mathbf Q[M_i]$ identify $J_i$ with $\mathbf Q[I_i]$ and each normalized blowup map with the realization of $M_{i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i}(M_i)^{\rm sat}$. Uniqueness is with these canonical centered chart identifications and the specified base $M$, not uniqueness among arbitrary scheme isomorphisms. If $X_n$ is regular, $M_n$ is smooth.

proof.text: Assume the final scheme is regular. Its realization isomorphism transports local Noetherianity by the open-immersion Noetherianity theorem. At each point its stalk map is a ring isomorphism, so IsRegularLocalRing.of_ringEquiv transports regularity to the realization stalk. Apply isSmooth_of_rational_realization_regular with the final torsion-freeness field. Its conclusion is definitionally Fine.IsSmooth. Pair this implication with the uniqueness conclusion for the chosen L.
